name: mint cilantro yogurt
instructions:
The green yogurt sauce — mint/cilantro/garlic/ginger in yogurt, with a pepper and a zucchini doing the structural work. BLENDER ONLY (a food processor isn't appropriate here — see notes).

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- NEUTRAL (PLAIN) YOGURT — best. Greek yogurt works but requires water, milk, or cream to thin it.
- MINT + CILANTRO
- GARLIC + GINGER
- A PEPPER — POBLANO or ANAHEIM. Necessary: it turns the sauce from vegetal to FUNKY (see notes).
- ZUCCHINI — for creaminess.
- SALT.

NO LIME — clashing; tasted surprisingly horrible (see notes).

=== PROCEDURE ===

Blend everything in a PROPER BLENDER until creamy.
notes:
=== THE CORE INSIGHT — THE CLASSIC FOUR AREN'T ENOUGH FOR A SAUCE ===

The classic mint/cilantro/garlic/ginger is enough for a CHICKEN MARINADE, but NOT for a creamy sauce — on its own it tastes too VEGETAL AND THIN. Two additions fix it:
1. A PEPPER (poblano/anaheim) — turns vegetal → FUNKY.
2. A ZUCCHINI — creaminess.
Which means this sauce follows MEXICAN MOLE VERDE LOGIC (green chile + green vegetable body) as well as SMOOTHIE LOGIC — it's not just thinned chutney.

=== YOGURT — NEUTRAL IS BEST ===

Neutral (plain) yogurt is best. GREEK yogurt requires water or milk or cream to loosen it — workable, but an extra step.

=== WANT TO TRY — CUCUMBER / AVOCADO IN THE ZUCCHINI SLOT ===

CUCUMBER and AVOCADO in place of the zucchini for creaminess. The worry with avocado: it won't STORE in the fridge — it'll oxidize without some kind of acid, and lime isn't good here (clashing). Unresolved whether the yogurt's own acidity is enough to hold it.

=== LIME IS CLASHING — SURPRISINGLY HORRIBLE ===

Lime tasted SURPRISINGLY horrible here. Clashing. (The yogurt is already the acid.)

=== BLENDER, NOT FOOD PROCESSOR ===

You need a PROPER BLENDER for this — a food processor isn't appropriate. (The inverse of [[relish]]'s coarse-pulse rule: this sauce wants to be fully creamy, and the processor can't get it there.)

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[mint-cilantro-chimichurri]]: the vinegar/oil expression of the herb pair — this is the yogurt expression.
- [[mint-cilantro-chicken]]: the herb-finish skillet (where the classic four DO suffice — on chicken, as a finish, not a sauce).
- [[jam-chutney]]: the sweet half of the dipping-sauce shelf; this is the green half.
- [[mexican-tofu-fritters]]: a landing spot — and the mole verde logic loops the sauce back toward that plate's register anyway.
original_chef: Mine — the classic green chutney rebuilt on mole-verde/smoothie logic.
